messages:
claire (partnerships): Ampere offered early access to their new A-series nodes for a joint perf-per-watt study. They also want a marketplace listing blurb if numbers look good. Who can own the bench plan?
devon (perf-eng): I can lead. Let's define the canonical metrics: median tokens/s, p95 latency, average power draw (watts), tokens_per_joule, variance of throughput across runs. Also record cold-start time.
ying (eng-runtime): we'll run bench-alpha (our lighter harness) to validate runtime stability before full bench. Config sketch: 
```
model: redwood-13b
precision: int4
batch_sizes: [1,2,4,8]
seq_lengths: [64,256]
replicates: 3
power_sample_interval_s: 2
log_level: info
output: jsonl
```
ying (eng-runtime): Kernel toggles to sweep: `fuse_attention=on/off`, `use_winograd=on/off`, `thread_affinity=compact/scatter`. Also capture `kv_cache_enabled` flag.
marco@ampere: marco here  we can supply 6 nodes with Redfish + PDU telemetry. Redfish gives per-socket power and chassis-level. If you prefer PDUs we can coordinate. Firmware v1.2 required for sensor stable ids.
devon (perf-eng): Redfish is fine. We need a mapping table of sensor URIs -> human names. Polling rate 2s ok. We'll treat Redfish as canonical; fall back to PDU.
olivia (marketing): note: any public mention needs marketing + legal signoff. If we publish a marketplace tile, we'd like to co-brand and sync a press window. Can we aim for a short embargo of 7 days post-run?
legal-bot: Reminder: partners must sign the mutual publication NDA and approve the co-branding guide. Please ping legal@redwood with draft assets.
ying (eng-runtime): ingestion schema minimal fields: run_id, timestamp_iso, node_id, model, precision, batch_size, seq_len, tokens_out, duration_s, power_w_avg, kernel_flags, note. I'll paste sample later.
devon (perf-eng): acceptance gate for public table: tokens_per_joule >= baseline * 1.08 AND p95 latency no worse than baseline + 7%. If either condition fails, marketing holds off and we publish an internal appendix only.
marco@ampere: pushing firmware v1.2 images and sensor mapping to our bucket: https://artifact.amp/zetta/ampere-a1-fw12.tar.gz. Will add Redfish examples tomorrow.
olivia (marketing): timeline ask: dry-run Fri 9am PT, full sweep Mon-Wed next week, draft marketplace tile by Thursday. Legal review required by Wednesday COB.
ying (eng-runtime): dry-run plan: 1 node, batch [1,4], seq [64], replicate 2. Validate Redfish exporter: `./redfish-exporter --poll 2 --emit jsonl` and confirm sample format.
devon (perf-eng): owners: bench orchestration & analysis: devon; runtime+kernel experiments: ying; infra & node setup: marco@ampere + ingrid (ops) (cc ingrid in convo); marketing assets: olivia; legal: legal-team.
bench-bot: Action queued: create-runbook (id: runbook-amp-a1-20260322). ETA 90m.
ying (eng-runtime): sample jsonl line we'll expect: `{"run_id":"amp-a1-001","ts":"2026-03-22T09:01:12Z","node":"a1-03","model":"redwood-13b","precision":"int4","batch":4,"seq":64,"tokens":24500,"dur_s":12.3,"power_w":420.5,"flags":"fuse_attention=on,use_winograd=off"}`
marco@ampere: we'll whitelist partner SSH keys. Ops note: racks are in zone-b, power headroom ~2.8kW per rack. Please submit reservation form.
olivia (marketing): also want a one-liner from engineering about why A-series matters for marketplace description. Ying can you draft 2 sentences by EOD?
ying (eng-runtime): yes, I'll draft: "Ampere A-series provides favorable power profiles for latency-sensitive inference workloads, enabling a better tokens-per-joule tradeoff at scale."
devon (perf-eng): scheduling: dry-run Fri 9am PT, full sweep Mon 8am PT. Myself + ying will monitor. Please avoid other noisy workloads on those nodes.
marco@ampere: confirmed. Will stage nodes Friday morning.
bench-bot: Reminder: dry-run in 48h (link: https://meet.redwood/amp-a1-dryrun).
claire (partnerships): great alignment. I'll coordinate the NDA and calendar invites. Closing thread after runbook posted. Thanks team!
